newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW-Samart focuses on mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Samart focuses on mobile phones.

text.p: Thai telecommunications firm Samart Corp Plc will focus on the mobile phone business in an attempt to capture more of the lucrative market, a senior company official said on Thursday.

"Most of our investment in the next few years will be in the mobile phone business. We aim to complete our nationwide mobile phone network within three years," Tom Kruesopon, director of corporate strategy, told Reuters in an interview.
"Mobile phone business has room to grow as only 2.9 percent of the total population already have mobile phone," he said.
Samart, via its mobile phone unit Digital Phone Co Ltd (DPC), plans to expand its digital mobile phone service in the first quarter of next year.
Digital Phone was awarded a concession by the government to operate digital mobile phones in the 1,800 mkz frequency.
"We expect to have 75,000 new subscribers in the first year. In the year 2000, our subcriber numbers are targeted to rise to 300,000," Tom said.
Total investment for the network would be about $600 million, most of which would be financed by borrowings, he said.
"Samart will contribute only $60 million funds into the projects. The remaining will be from our partner and loans," he added.
Samart and Malaysian state-run telephone company Telekom Malaysia Bhd early last month signed a deal for the Malaysian firm to buy a 20.12 percent in Samart Corp for $71.5 million.
Telekom Malaysia also bought a 33.3 percent stake in DPC for $135 million.
"Telekom Malaysia is a major telecommunications company in Asia. Its expertise and experience in international telecommunications market will also help expand Samart's overseas businesses," Tom said.
Samart was very optimistic about Cambodia, where the company is the leading mobile phone operator, despite the political turmoil, Tom said.
"As long as Cambodia remains a democratic country, telecommunications business there remains attractive," he said.

Samart also plans to invest in the telecommunications industry in Burma due to the country's underdeveloped telecommunications infrastructure and its expected admission to the Association of South East Asian National (ASEAN).
"Burma is one of our prime focuses now. It's telecommunications infrastructure is severely underdeveloped and its admission to ASEAN will help boost its economy in the long term," he said.
ASEAN said in May it would admit Burma together with Cambodia and Laos as a new member in July.
ASEAN currently comprises Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
